method: Each page was fetched on the check date and the sentences the article relies on were located in the page text. Findings are paraphrased here; the pages themselves are the source. The one-line rules in the article are our own wording, not quotations from any of these pages.

origin.name: The Inner Circle Trader, home page
what_it_says: Written in the first person; the author introduces himself as Michael J. Huddleston, otherwise known as The Inner Circle Trader, and addresses new and aspiring forex traders.
Links to a YouTube channel (youtube.com/innercircletrader) and, under 'ICT Mentorship Core Content', to a YouTube playlist.
does_not_say: None of the twelve terms in the article appears on this page.
No years, no track record, no statement of when any term was introduced.

origin.name: YouTube playlist linked from that page
what_it_says: Playlist title: '2016 ICT Private Mentorship Core Content Month 01'.
origin.caveat: We read the title only. We have not watched the lectures and do not attribute any term to a specific video.

origin.name: YouTube channel linked from that page
what_it_says: Channel name: The Inner Circle Trader.

origin.name: TradingView: Smart Money Concepts (SMC) [LuxAlgo], open-source script
what_it_says: Calls 'Smart Money Concepts' a fairly new yet widely used term, coined and popularised primarily within the forex community and by ICT.
States there is no supporting data regarding the validity of these teachings.

Features listed: internal and swing structure with BOS and CHoCH labels, order blocks (removed when price breaks through, i.e. mitigated), equal highs and lows, fair value gaps, premium and discount zones.

origin.name: LuxAlgo library: Smart Money Concepts
what_it_says: ICT is Michael J. Huddleston's own body of teaching; SMC is the community's label for the same core ideas, often with renamed or simplified terms.
The ideas predate the branding (Wyckoff on accumulation and distribution; supply-and-demand zones before the 'order block' label).
No rigorous public study shows the methodology is profitable on its own; patterns are defined loosely enough that two traders can mark the same chart differently.
The last candle that closed against a move before the move took off; the candle alone is not the concept, the displacement after it is required.
Drawing conventions vary and none is official (full range, body only, open to extreme, 50% of the range).
No reliable universal hit rate exists.
An order block that failed and flipped roles.
Two readings circulate: the strict one requires the failing swing to first trade beyond a prior high or low; the looser one treats any violated order block as a breaker.
A with-trend structural break.
A body close beyond the level is the common filter; wick-based readings also exist.
Usage of the terms varies by author.

concepts.concept: change of character / market structure shift
what_it_says: The first structural break against the prevailing trend.
Vocabulary is not fully standardized: many use CHoCH and MSS interchangeably, others reserve MSS for a counter-trend break with displacement right after a liquidity sweep of the trend's extreme.
A fair value gap that failed and flipped roles; the common requirement is a body close beyond the far side of the gap.
Conventions differ on strictness: whole gap closed through, or a close beyond its midpoint.

New York time: Asian roughly 8:00 to 10:00 pm, London open 2:00 to 5:00 am, New York AM 7:00 to 10:00 am (index-futures variants 8:30 to 11:00), London close 10:00 am to 12:00 pm, New York PM 1:30 to 4:00 pm.
Window boundaries differ by 30 to 90 minutes across ICT sources and platforms.
The false move early in a session that runs resting stops before the day's real move goes the other way; measured against the midnight New York opening price.
Confirmed by the failure, never assumed from the clock; stated windows vary across different series of teachings.
A template for how a trading period unfolds around its open: accumulation, manipulation, distribution.
Easy to see in hindsight on a finished candle; descriptive, not mechanical.
Open-source script that says it is inspired from the lectures of The Inner Circle Trader.
Three windows in New York local time: 3 to 4 am, 10 to 11 am, 2 to 3 pm; a fair value gap has to form inside the window.
Sets a minimum distance of 40 ticks for index futures and 15 pips for forex pairs; advises timeframes below 15 minutes.
No audited public statistics exist; win rates circulating online should be treated as marketing until shown otherwise.
See research/liquidity-sweep/liquidity-sweep_sources.json.
Most tools require a minimum size (ATR or percentage); many treat a touch of the midpoint as a fill. Cited in en/fair-value-gap.

not_found: A dated primary source for the first use of each of the twelve terms. The definitions live in years of video lectures, which we have not catalogued.
Who first used 'Smart Money Concepts' as a label.
Any audited or independently verified performance record for the method as a whole.
Any figure for what share of people who trade this way make money.
source_caveat: Most concept descriptions above come from LuxAlgo, a company that sells charting indicators. It is not the originator of the vocabulary. We use its library because it states rules precisely and says where conventions differ.
